items.claim: The row's central inclusio argument for closing the poem at 3.18 quotes no Hebrew word at all for 3.18's half of the pair, and its claim that 3.19-20's earth/heaven-founding clause is governed by 'אֶל' cited from 3.5 is wrong: the actual subject of both verbs in 3.19 is יְֽהוָ֗ה, not the preposition אֶל.
items.evidence: (1) The rationale's inclusio claim -- '3.18, which closes with (oshb:Prov.3.18), a participle sharing the same root as the opening אַשְׁרֵ֣י' -- leaves the Hebrew slot for 3.18 blank (two spaces, no token: verified at the byte level). The underlying claim is TRUE (3.18 ends מְאֻשָּֽׁר, a Pual participle sharing its root with אַשְׁרֵ֣י opening 3.13 -- collate.py confirms both cited forms byte-match their own verses), but per the OL lens a Hebrew claim with no quoted form is insufficient engagement: the row never actually quotes מְאֻשָּֽׁר. (2) Separately, the rationale glosses 3.19-20 as 'אֶל (oshb:Prov.3.5) founding the earth and establishing the heavens.' oshb:Prov.3.5 reads 'בְּטַ֣ח אֶל יְ֭הוָה בְּכָל לִבֶּ֑ךָ וְאֶל בִּֽ֝ינָתְךָ֗ אַל תִּשָּׁעֵֽן' -- אֶל there is the preposition 'to/toward' (segol-pointed), occurring twice, governing 'trust TOWARD YHWH' and 'lean not TOWARD your own understanding'; it is not a name for God and does not occur in 3.19-20 at all. oshb:Prov.3.19 reads 'יְֽהוָ֗ה בְּחָכְמָ֥ה יָֽסַד אָ֑רֶץ כּוֹנֵ֥ן שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם בִּתְבוּנָֽה' -- its subject is יְֽהוָ֗ה (YHWH), not אֶל. The citation misidentifies the acting subject of the cosmic-scope couplet the row uses to justify extending the poem through 3.20.

collate: oshb:Prov.3.18 = no quote present (none tier / insufficient engagement)

byte-check: oshb:Prov.3.19 word1 = יְֽהוָ֗ה (actual subject of founding/establishing verbs)

items.claim: device_notes asserts a synonymous 'eyes/heart' word-pair at 3.21, but 'heart' does not occur anywhere in 3.21 -- the row's own opening verse, which names only מֵעֵינֶ֑יךָ ('your eyes') -- and the rationale repeats the same mislocated אֶל citation from 3.5 used elsewhere in the cluster.
items.evidence: (1) device_notes reads 'Synonymous parallelism (eyes/heart at 3.21 continuing into life/grace at 3.22...)'. oshb:Prov.3.21 is 'בְּ֭נִי אַל יָלֻ֣זוּ מֵעֵינֶ֑יךָ נְצֹ֥ר תֻּ֝שִׁיָּ֗ה וּמְזִמָּֽה' -- it contains only 'your eyes' (מֵעֵינֶ֑יךָ), never 'heart'; the heart word (לִבֶּֽךָ) belongs to the PRECEDING unit's own verses (oshb:Prov.3.1 ends לִבֶּֽךָ; oshb:Prov.3.3 ends לִבֶּֽךָ), outside this row's 3.21-3.26 span. The claimed pair is fabricated at the byte level. (2) The rationale and device_notes both cite 'אֶל (oshb:Prov.3.5)' as governing 3.25-26 ('because אֶל is the addressee's confidence' / 'names אֶל explicitly as the ground of confidence') -- the same mislocated preposition-as-subject error found in P02-003 and P02-006: oshb:Prov.3.26 reads 'כִּֽי יְ֭הוָה יִהְיֶ֣ה בְכִסְלֶ֑ךָ וְשָׁמַ֖ר רַגְלְךָ֣ מִלָּֽכֶד', subject יְ֭הוָה (YHWH), never אֶל (which belongs to 3.5 and means 'to/toward', not 'the LORD').

items.claim: The rationale's central content description -- four gnomic sayings 'pairing אֶל (oshb:Prov.3.5)'s disposition with a human outcome' -- misidentifies the acting subject: the same mislocated preposition-from-3.5 error found in P02-003 and P02-004, though the row's actual boundary drivers (the 3.32 conjunction and the 3.35 petuchah) are independently correct.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.3.32 reads 'כִּ֤י תוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֣ה נָל֑וֹז וְֽאֶת יְשָׁרִ֥ים סוֹדֽוֹ' -- it explicitly names יְהוָ֣ה (YHWH, word index 2: 'the abomination of YHWH is the perverse man'), and oshb:Prov.3.33 opens 'מְאֵרַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה' ('the curse of YHWH'), also YHWH-named. אֶל never occurs in 3.32-35; it is the preposition quoted from oshb:Prov.3.5 ('trust TOWARD YHWH'), not a name for the deity, and does not carry a 'disposition' of its own. The mark/kq disclosures for this row (petuchah after 3.35, ketiv/qere at 3.34) are independently correct against pmarks_Prov.json, and the conjunction opening 3.32 is byte-confirmed as the discourse-turn marker -- the boundary call survives, but the row's characterization of what the four sayings pair together is wrong.

items.claim: The rationale's 'echoed again at the head of 4.7' description overstates the byte-level position of the repetition: 4.7 opens with a different word, and the two get-imperatives from 4.5 recur split apart (near-start and at the tail of 4.7) rather than as one contiguous re-echoed phrase.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.4.7 reads 'רֵאשִׁ֣ית חָ֭כְמָה קְנֵ֣ה חָכְמָ֑ה וּבְכָל קִ֝נְיָנְךָ֗ קְנֵ֣ה בִינָֽה'; its actual head word is רֵאשִׁ֣ית ('beginning'), not the quoted imperative. The 4.5 phrase 'קְנֵ֣ה חָ֭כְמָה קְנֵ֣ה בִינָ֑ה אַל תִּשְׁכַּ֥ח וְאַל תֵּ֝֗ט מֵֽאִמְרֵי פִֽי' ('get wisdom, get understanding') does recur as two separate word-pairs inside 4.7 -- get-wisdom as 4.7's 3rd-4th words, get-understanding as its final two words -- but they are split by an intervening clause ('and with all your getting'), not adjacent as 'echoed at the head' implies. The underlying repetition-based cohesion argument for keeping 4.5-4.9 together is still real (both two-word imperatives do recur verbatim within the row's own span), so this is a positional-precision defect rather than a fabricated device.

items.claim: The rejected_alternative's stated reason for not narrowing the row -- that all four verses 4.16-19 'share one grammatical subject ("the wicked"/"they") running continuously' -- is byte-false at 4.18, which switches to 'the path of the righteous' as its subject, directly contradicting the row's own device_notes two sentences later that correctly calls 4.18-19 antithetic.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.4.16-17 do share a continuous 'they' subject (wicked, verbal). But oshb:Prov.4.18 opens 'וְאֹ֣רַח צַ֭דִּיקִים...' ('the path of the righteous'), a nominal subject naming the OPPOSITE referent, not 'the wicked/they'; oshb:Prov.4.19 opens 'דֶּ֣רֶךְ רְ֭שָׁעִים...' ('the way of the wicked'), switching back. The row's own device_notes independently (and correctly) calls 4.18-19 'antithetic parallelism... (light/darkness...)', which by definition requires contrasting, not continuous, subjects -- so the row contradicts itself. The row's PRIMARY rationale for the span (the shared 'path to avoid' object distinguishing it from 4.10-13) is unaffected and independently sound; the defect is confined to the secondary rejected_alternative justification. All disclosure-object citations (ketiv/qere at 4.16, petuchah after 4.19) remain independently byte-correct.
